quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #8
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: A driver's left arm and hand are extended upward. What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Turn left.
Turn right.
Come to a stop.
Go straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn right.
questions.explanation: When a driver's left arm and hand point upward, they are signaling a right turn. If you are following this driver, be ready for them to turn right.

questions.question: Which is a dangerous habit when driving in work zones?

options.text: Tailgating another vehicle
Failing to carefully watch for workers and moving equipment
Both of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above
questions.explanation: In work zones, slow down and do not follow other vehicles too closely. Always watch for workers and equipment on the road.

questions.question: Which lane should you be in before turning left from a one-way street?

options.text: The lane nearest the left curb.
The lane nearest the center of the street.
The lane nearest the right curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane nearest the left curb.
questions.explanation: Always turn from the lane closest to the direction you want to go. For a left turn on a one-way street, use the lane nearest the left curb.

questions.question: What affects your ability to stop?

options.text: Signal lights.
Other cars on the road.
The time of day.
The condition of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The condition of the road.
questions.explanation: Road condition greatly affects how quickly you can stop. Slow down on slippery or poor road conditions so you can maintain control and stop safely.

questions.question: Fog reduces visibility of other vehicles, pedestrians, and traffic signals. When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Drive cautiously and reduce your speed.
Not use your high beam headlights.
Use low beam headlights to better see the road and objects ahead.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: In fog, drive carefully and slowly. Do not use high beams because they reflect off the fog. Use low beams instead, which light up the road better in foggy conditions.

questions.question: Your power steering stops working while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn and turn off the ignition.
Turn on your hazard lights and brace yourself.
Steer with extra effort, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.
Slam on your brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer with extra effort, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.
questions.explanation: Without power steering, you need to steer harder. Reduce speed and carefully drive to a safe spot off the road to stop.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You must travel through the intersection at the posted speed limit.
The maximum speed limit under ideal conditions is 55 mph.
You must not travel below the speed indicated.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum speed limit under ideal conditions is 55 mph.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the maximum speed allowed on that road. You can drive slower based on road conditions, but you cannot drive faster than this limit.

questions.question: A steady yellow traffic light means the red light is coming soon. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, what should you do?

options.text: Stop.
Continue moving and clear the intersection safely.
Speed up to avoid an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue moving and clear the intersection safely.
questions.explanation: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, continue through safely and clear the intersection as quickly as possible.

questions.question: How can you avoid making emergency stops while driving in traffic?

options.text: Honk your horn to alert other drivers.
Look ahead and keep a safe distance from other vehicles.
Drive in the right lane only.
Drive more slowly than other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and keep a safe distance from other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Maintaining a safe following distance gives you time to react to problems ahead without emergency braking, which could cause a crash from the driver behind you.

questions.question: On a multilane road, a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:

options.text: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed only from the side with the dashed line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed only from the side with the dashed line.
questions.explanation: When there is a dashed yellow line and a solid yellow line, only drivers on the dashed line side may pass. Drivers on the solid line side cannot pass.

questions.question: When entering a street from a driveway, you:

options.text: Must drive slowly to give approaching vehicles and pedestrians time to move.
Must honk your horn so approaching vehicles and pedestrians know you are coming.
Must stop and only proceed when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching.
Can ignore pedestrians if there is no sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop and only proceed when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching.
questions.explanation: Always stop before entering the street from a driveway. Yield to any approaching vehicles or crossing pedestrians. Stop before crossing the sidewalk. Not stopping is against the law.

questions.question: If an oncoming driver does not dim their headlights, you should:

options.text: Look toward the center of the road.
Look toward the right side of the road.
Look straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: If an oncoming driver does not dim their headlights, look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded and lets you see enough road to stay on course. Do not retaliate by keeping your bright lights on.

questions.question: If a red light is showing and a police officer tells you to go through the intersection, you should:

options.text: Stop until the light turns green.
Go through the intersection without stopping.
Come to a complete stop before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go through the intersection without stopping.
questions.explanation: A police officer's directions always override traffic signals and signs. Follow the officer's instructions.

questions.question: Which factor affects how your body absorbs alcohol?

options.text: Weight
Height
Intelligence

questions.correctAnswerText: Weight
questions.explanation: Factors that affect alcohol absorption include body weight, biological sex, food in your stomach, and how many drinks you have consumed. The only way to remove alcohol from your system is to wait.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Slow-moving vehicle.
Road construction or maintenance ahead.
Traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle.
questions.explanation: This sign is displayed on vehicles that move slowly.

questions.question: When approaching an accident scene, you should:

options.text: Keep your attention on your driving.
Keep moving.
Stop if you are involved or if emergency help has not yet arrived.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not stop at an accident unless you are involved or emergency help has not arrived. Keep your attention on driving and keep moving. Watch for people on or near the road. Do not drive to accidents, fires, or disasters just to look.

questions.question: A driver should:

options.text: Assume all drivers obey right-of-way rules.
Assume most drivers obey right-of-way rules.
Always be ready to give up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to give up the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Right-of-way rules are a guide, but no one should assume they automatically have the right-of-way. Always consider the situation and circumstances at an intersection. Yield your legal right-of-way if it helps prevent a collision.

questions.question: At an intersection with a yield sign, you should:

options.text: Always stop before entering the intersection.
Yield only to traffic on the right.
Yield only to traffic on the left.
Slow down and yield the right-of-way to other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield the right-of-way to other traffic.
questions.explanation: A yield sign means you must slow down and give the right-of-way to traffic in the intersection or roadway you are entering.

questions.question: As you enter a roundabout, you should slow down and:

options.text: Yield to pedestrians and bicyclists.
Yield to cars already in the roundabout.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and traffic already in the roundabout.

questions.question: If two drivers arrive at the same time to an open intersection:

options.text: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
The driver on the left has the right-of-way.
One driver may continue without stopping.
One driver should honk to show they are giving up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: If you arrive at an open intersection at the same time as a vehicle on your right, yield to that vehicle. Then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: If a driver is worried, nervous, angry, or crying, they should:

options.text: Drive normally because emotions do not affect driving.
Drive faster because they are more alert.
Calm down and focus before starting to drive.
Call a friend to talk while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Calm down and focus before starting to drive.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions can distract you from driving safely. Your attention will be on your feelings instead of the road. Always take time to calm down and focus before you start driving.

questions.question: When driving behind another vehicle at night, you should:

options.text: Use low beam headlights.
Use high beam headlights until you are 10 feet from the vehicle.
Use high beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use high beams only in rural areas when no other cars are near. Switch to low beams when following another vehicle closely.

questions.question: On slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Slow down.
Drive faster.
Drive at the speed limit with caution.
Not drive faster than 20 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down when rain, snow, or sleet makes roads slippery. Drive slower than the speed limit if conditions are poor.

questions.question: In very heavy fog, you should slow down and:

options.text: Turn on your emergency flashers.
Use high beam headlights.
Use low beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off water droplets and create glare, making it harder to see. Some vehicles have fog lights that work with low beams.

questions.question: When riding in a vehicle, small children:

options.text: Can be safely held by an adult.
Are safe standing on the floor in the back.
Will not be hurt in an accident because they are small.
Must be properly secured in a child seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must be properly secured in a child seat.
questions.explanation: Children must always be in proper child seats. No adult is strong enough to hold a child safely during a crash or sudden stop.

questions.question: You have a green light but traffic is blocking the intersection. You should:

options.text: Turn left and find another route.
Wait until the intersection clears.
Enter the intersection with the other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the intersection clears.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection if other vehicles are blocking it, even with a green light. If you enter and the light turns red, you will block cross traffic and may get a ticket.

questions.question: Drowsy drivers:

options.text: Can stay awake by drinking strong coffee.
May drive as poorly as a drunk driver.
Can stay alert by opening a window and turning up the radio.
Are usually only older drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: May drive as poorly as a drunk driver.
questions.explanation: Drowsy drivers can drive so poorly that they look drunk. Opening a window, turning on the radio, or drinking coffee is not enough to keep a drowsy driver alert.

questions.question: Which statement is true about alcohol and driving?

options.text: If you can walk in a straight line, you can safely drive.
If you are below the legal alcohol limit, your driving is safe.
Alcohol affects your judgment, which you need to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol affects your judgment, which you need to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects your judgment. Good judgment helps you react safely to what you see and hear on the road. Any amount of alcohol can affect your driving ability.

questions.question: You are driving behind a motorcycle and want to pass. You must:

options.text: Stay in the right lane because the motorcycle is small.
Honk your horn to make the motorcycle move over.
Move completely into the left lane before and during the pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move completely into the left lane before and during the pass.
questions.explanation: Give a motorcycle a full lane when passing. Do not share the lane. If you move back too soon, the rider may swerve into traffic or off the road.

questions.question: Before passing another vehicle, you should signal:

options.text: Just before changing lanes.
At any time.
After changing lanes.
Early so other drivers know your plan.

questions.correctAnswerText: Early so other drivers know your plan.
questions.explanation: Signal early before passing. Other drivers need time to know what you plan to do.

questions.question: What should you do to prevent hydroplaning?

options.text: Keep your tires with good tread depth.
Keep your tires inflated to the correct pressure.
Slow down when driving in rain.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: To prevent hydroplaning, keep your tires with good tread and proper air pressure. Slow down when driving in rain. Hydroplaning happens most often at high speeds.

questions.question: Who must yield when a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light?

options.text: Whoever started moving last.
The driver.
Whoever is slower.
The pedestrian.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver.
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing at any intersection without a traffic light, with or without a crosswalk.

questions.question: When can you legally drive around or under a railroad crossing gate?

options.text: Never.
When you can see clearly in both directions.
When the warning lights are not flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never drive around or under a lowered railroad gate. Once the gate is raised, wait until you can see clearly in both directions and are sure no trains are coming before crossing the tracks.

questions.question: What does drinking coffee after drinking alcohol do?

options.text: Lowers blood alcohol concentration.
Stops the effects of alcohol.
Has no effect on blood alcohol concentration.
Raises blood alcohol concentration.

questions.correctAnswerText: Has no effect on blood alcohol concentration.
questions.explanation: Coffee will not lower your blood alcohol level. It may help you stay awake, but it cannot change your blood alcohol level or make you sober.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spot before changing lanes?

options.text: Look in the left side mirror.
Look in the right side mirror.
Look in the rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulder toward the direction you want to move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder toward the direction you want to move.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to check your blind spot.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow centerline mean?

options.text: Passing is not allowed.
You can pass on the right when the road is clear.
You can pass on the left when the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass on the left when the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow centerline means you can cross it to pass another vehicle on the left if no cars are coming. Never cross a solid yellow centerline to pass.

questions.question: What can a bicyclist do when making a left turn?

options.text: They can use the left lane.
They can cut through all lanes.
They can wait on the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can use the left lane.
questions.explanation: Expect to see bicyclists riding with traffic on the road. A bicyclist may use the left lane when turning left.

questions.question: Lanes moving in the same direction are divided by ____ lines.

options.text: Yellow.
White.
Red.
Black.

questions.correctAnswerText: White.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and mark the right edge of the road. Broken white lines can be crossed to pass. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: Why should you use your headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days?

options.text: To keep your engine warm.
So other drivers can see your vehicle.
To warn others about bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: So other drivers can see your vehicle.
questions.explanation: In rain, snow, or fog, other drivers have trouble seeing your vehicle. Headlights make your vehicle easier to see. If you use your windshield wipers, you must also turn on your low beam headlights.

questions.question: What should you do when driving near a large commercial vehicle?

options.text: Follow closely to reduce wind drag on your vehicle.
Avoid driving beside it for long periods of time.
Drive on its right side on curves and hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid driving beside it for long periods of time.
questions.explanation: Large commercial vehicles have big blind spots on each side. Avoid driving beside them for long periods of time.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Road construction or maintenance area ahead.
Side road ahead.
Railroad ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road construction or maintenance area ahead.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn drivers of hazards. Orange signs warn of construction or maintenance work ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for bicycles.
Bicycles are not allowed.
Bicycle repair shop ahead.
Bicycles have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for bicycles.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that bicycles may be in the area.

questions.question: When should you allow extra space between your vehicle and others?

options.text: When following a station wagon.
When following a driver who cannot see the rear of their vehicle.
When following a small passenger car.

questions.correctAnswerText: When following a driver who cannot see the rear of their vehicle.
questions.explanation: Drivers of trucks, buses, vans, and vehicles towing trailers may not be able to see you directly behind them. Stay farther back so they can see you. Large vehicles also block your view of the road ahead, so more distance helps you see around them.

questions.question: What does this sign tell you about the road ahead?

options.text: The road turns sharply right, then left.
The road curves right, then left.
The road curves right.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road will curve right and then curve left.

questions.question: What does this yellow warning sign mean?

options.text: You are near a school or school crosswalk.
Slow down and watch for children.
Both A and B.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both A and B.
questions.explanation: This sign is placed on roads near schools to warn drivers to slow down and watch for children.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines mean?

options.text: No vehicle may pass.
Both lanes may pass.
The right lane may pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: No vehicle may pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions. Double solid yellow lines mean passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.question: You see a railroad crossbuck sign but no gates or lights. What should you do?

options.text: Be very careful and cross only when you are sure no train is coming.
Turn off your radio to listen for a train.
Wait for a flagger's signal before crossing if one is present.
Do all of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do all of the above.
questions.explanation: Always approach railroad crossings with caution and cross only when you know no train is coming. Listen for trains by lowering your radio volume. Follow all instructions from a flagger if one is present.

questions.question: What can you do on a road with a single broken white centerline?

options.text: You must stay in your lane.
You may cross it to change lanes.
You may change lanes only from the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may cross it to change lanes.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A broken white line means you may pass another vehicle when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What happens when drivers slow down to look at crashes or unusual sights?

options.text: It causes traffic to back up.
It prevents rear-end crashes.
It improves traffic flow.

questions.correctAnswerText: It causes traffic to back up.
questions.explanation: Avoid looking at crashes or unusual sights while driving. This slowing down, called "rubbernecking," causes traffic congestion.

questions.question: What is distracted driving?

options.text: Anything that makes you swerve while driving.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you focus more on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving means anything that takes your eyes, hands, or mind off the road. It is a leading cause of traffic crashes. Any distraction prevents you from noticing hazards and reacting safely.
